title: Early Planet Formation in Embedded Disks (eDisk). XII. Accretion Streamers, Protoplanetary Disk, and Outflow in the Class I Source Oph IRS 63
question: Characterize the gas and dust structures, kinematics, accretion streamers, and mass budget (envelope infall versus stellar accretion) of the Class I source Oph IRS63 in the context of early planet formation.

what.value: Distance to Oph IRS63 of 132 ± 6 pc

evidence.quote: The distance to Oph IRS63 is estimated to be $132 \pm 6$ pc based on its proximity to the B45 molecular cloud (cite: Zucker2020).

what.value: Bolometric temperature (T_bol = 348 K) and bolometric luminosity (L_bol = 1.3 L_sun)

evidence.quote: The bolometric temperature and luminosity of Oph IRS63 ($\rm T_{bol}$=348 K and $\rm L_{bol}$=1.3 $\rm L_\odot$), make it the most evolved source (closer to the Class II phase) of the whole eDisk sample (cite: Ohashi2023)

what.value: Rotational constant B_e of C18O from the JPL database

evidence.quote: Using a standard abundance of $3 \times 10^{-7}$ (cite: Frerking1982) for C$^{18}$O and $B_e$ value taken from the JPL database (cite: Pickett1998), we obtain a total C$^{18}$O mass of $M_{envelope} \sim 0.04~M_\odot$.

what.value: 12CO column densities (2-5 x 10^18 cm^-2) and veiling (r_k = 3) from iSHELL observations

evidence.quote: Flores et al. (submitted) measured $^{12}$CO column densities of $2 - 5 \times$ 10$^{18}$ cm$^{-2}$
where the spectrum of Oph IRS63 is fit using a black body component (with a fixed veiling of $\rm r_{k}=3$, based on iSHELL observations)

recipe.goal: Measure basic dust continuum properties and dust disk size
recipe.method: Fit a 2D Gaussian profile in the image plane using CASA imfit to obtain center coordinates, position angle, and inclination; integrate flux density above 5 sigma; compute azimuthally averaged intensity profiles using GoFish to derive radii enclosing 68%, 90%, and 95% of total flux.
key_parameters: Flux integration threshold = 5 sigma; i = 47 deg; P.A. = 149 deg
assumptions: Thin axisymmetric disk geometry transforming deconvolved aspect ratio 0.685 to inclination 46.7 deg

recipe.method: Apply the Hildebrand (1983) optically thin thermal dust emission formula at 225 GHz using two dust temperature prescriptions.
key_parameters: nu = 225 GHz; S_nu = 317 mJy; D = 132 pc; T_dust = 20 K and 46 K
assumptions: Optically thin thermal emission; dust opacity kappa_nu = 2.3 cm^2 g^-1 of dust; D = 132 pc; L_bol = 1.3 L_sun

recipe.goal: Generate moment maps and characterize molecular emission morphology
recipe.method: Create moment 0 (integrated intensity), moment 1 (velocity), and moment 8 (peak intensity) maps of 12CO, 13CO, C18O, SO, and H2CO; fit a 2D Gaussian to the SO ring central depression to measure its offset from the continuum peak.

recipe.goal: Kinematic analysis of the disk and envelope via Position-Velocity (PV) diagrams
recipe.method: Extract PV cuts along the disk major axis (5-pixel wide or ~0.5'') for 13CO, C18O, and SO; fit broken power-law (13CO, SO) or single power-law (C18O) rotation profiles using SLAM in both ridge and edge modes with MCMC to determine inner power-law index, break radius R_b, outer power-law index, systemic velocity, and dynamical stellar mass M_star.
key_parameters: PV cut width = 5 pixels (~0.5''); P.A. = 149 deg; emission threshold > 5 sigma; filtered-out velocity channels excluded
assumptions: d = 132 pc; i = 47 deg; Keplerian rotation forced to derive M_star

recipe.goal: Model C18O and SO spiral/arc structures as infalling rotating streamers
recipe.method: Apply the Mendoza et al. (2009) analytical ballistic model of a finite-sized rotating cloud collapsing onto a central point mass; manually adjust initial polar angle theta, azimuthal angle phi, and cloud radius R_cloud to visually match projected 2D trajectories and PV diagram velocity profiles for 3 C18O streamers and 3 SO spirals.
key_parameters: M_star = 0.5 M_sun; i = 47 deg; P.A. = 149 deg; near side = 59 deg E of N; For C18O: R_disk = 265 au, R_cloud = 5300 au, h_0 = 1250 au km s^-1, (theta, phi) = (57, 188), (85, 270), (108, 300) deg; For SO: R_disk = 110 au, R_cloud = 550, 275, 1320 au, (theta, phi) = (124, 260), (55, 155), (67, 75) deg
assumptions: Negligible pressure gradient (supersonic flow); rigid-body rotation at spherical cloud boundary; negligible self-gravity (central star dominates); aligned cloud and disk rotational axes

recipe.goal: Derive envelope mass and envelope-to-disk mass infall rate
recipe.method: Verify C18O is optically thin and 13CO is optically thick using their brightness temperature ratio; compute gas excitation temperature T_ex from peak 13CO brightness temperature assuming LTE; compute C18O column density and total H2 envelope mass (excluding inner 265 au disk); divide envelope mass by free-fall infall timescale from the outermost C18O edge to the disk.
key_parameters: T_bg = 2.7 K; T_ex = 21 K; inner disk exclusion radius = 265 au; d = 132 pc
assumptions: LTE; optically thick 13CO and optically thin C18O; [12C]/[13C] = 77 and [16O]/[18O] = 560; X(C18O)/X(H2) = 3 x 10^-7; free-fall velocity from outermost edge

recipe.goal: Measure protostellar mass accretion rate and evaluate disk gravitational stability (Toomre Q) and gas-to-dust size ratio
recipe.method: De-redden IRTF iSHELL/SpeX spectra using A_v = 24 mag; integrate Br-gamma line flux at 2.166 um; convert Br-gamma luminosity to accretion luminosity via Alcalá et al. (2017) relation and derive stellar mass accretion rate; compute Toomre Q parameter using gas disk mass (from dust mass with g/d = 100) and gas radius R_gas = 265 au; compute ratio of gas disk radius to 95% dust continuum radius.
key_parameters: A_v = 24 mag (varied 20-40 mag); R_in = 5 R_star; R_star = 3.0 R_sun (varied 2.0-3.7 R_sun, log g = 3.2); M_star = 0.5 M_sun; T_eff = 3500 K; mu = 2.3; g/d = 100; T = 20 K and 46 K
assumptions: Alcalá et al. (2017) Br-gamma scaling (a = 1.19 ± 0.1, b = 4.02 ± 0.51); Fitzpatrick (1999) extinction law; gas-to-dust ratio = 100; mean molecular weight mu = 2.3

score_reason: The ALMA data are public in the archive, the core kinematic and continuum analysis tools (CASA, GoFish, SLAM) are public and well-cited, and the analytical equations and fitted parameters are explicitly tabulated. However, imaging details are deferred to the survey overview paper (Ohashi et al. 2023), the IRTF NIR spectra are not publicly linked, and the region definitions for the C18O infall rate and v_0 for streamer trajectories are not specified.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA datasets (2015.1.01512.S and 2019.A.00034.S) are public, and the primary ALMA-based results—continuum flux and radii (GoFish/imfit), dynamical stellar mass and gas disk break radius (SLAM on 13CO/C18O/SO), and streamer trajectory parameters—are numeric and can be reproduced directly from the visibility data or cubes.
